blocks.text: The atoms, molecules or ions of a solid substance are closely packed. The particles of solids cannot move closer to each other unlike gases. It is true for metallic solids that their atoms are spherically symmetrical. So, when such particles are arranged, they can give birth to hexagonal and cubic close-packed structures. Here outer boundaries of constituent particles touch each other but due to their spherical shapes, they cannot occupy more than 74% space. It means the compression of solids is not possible.
